script: Japan turned convenience stores into survival machines. In most countries, a convenience store is where you grab chips, a drink, and leave. But in Japan, the konbini is basically a tiny life-support system. You can buy fresh meals, hot coffee, clean socks, concert tickets, printer copies, umbrellas, phone chargers, and pay your bills before work. At midnight, when the city feels empty, the konbini is still glowing. A tired salaryman walks in for dinner. A student buys breakfast before the train. Someone grabs an umbrella because the rain came out of nowhere. And somehow, the food is not just emergency food. The egg sandwiches, rice balls, fried chicken, bento boxes, and desserts are actually good. That is why Japan's convenience stores feel different. They are not just stores. They are quiet little rescue stations on almost every corner.
title: The Great Emu War
